scope: Theorem 3.1 (Robust deletion estimates) of the manuscript “Balanced counterexamples to Ryser's conjecture at prime orders” (preprints/Balanced-Counterexamples-to-Rysers-Conjecture-at-Prime-Orders-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 162 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5be7cf2d1f382e80), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix k ≥ 1 and K ≥ 0. For each q, let Qq be a probability law on the same sets as Uq,k such that Qq(D) ≤ eKq Uq,k(D) for every D. Then the following assertions hold as q → ∞. (i) The empirical probability measure q−2 ∑︁ x∈A δiD(x) converges in probability, in total variation, to the Poisson distribution with mean k. (ii) Write µ = e−k. For every fixed λ, η > 0, the probability that at least ηq lines ℓ ∈ L \ D satisfy ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ |ℓ ∩ RD| q − µ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ≥ λ tends to zero. (iii) For every fixed δ > 0, the probability that there is a set C ⊆ L \ D with |C| ≤ q which covers RD and leaves at least δq2 points of A uncovered tends to zero.
